newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Buyers boost Australian stocks to higher end.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Buyers boost Australian stocks to higher end.

text.p: SPI Futures 2492 +14 US 30yr cl 6.53 -0.10
10yrbond futs 92.705 +0.030 Gold NY 344.25 Lon Fix 342.50
*Stocks close higher as buyers chase yields in big banks.
CBA active as goes ex-dividend. Volume 360.47 million, value A$801.38 million, 1,145 traded, 356 steady, 453 up, 336 down.
A confident Australian share market closed higher on Monday, helped by investors chasing the yields among the big banks.
Commonwealth Bank of Australia was the exception in the bank sector. The bank's stock slid 53 cents after to A$13.37 after it went ex-dividend 45 cents.
By 4.25 p.m. (0525 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 10.6 points higher at 2,493.2.
The March share price index futures contract was 14 points higher at 2,492, a 1.2 point discount to the underlying index.
"Generally, the market looks relatively strong," said dealer Peter Struk of Reynolds and Co.
"There has been buying right across the board and there has been nothing that has really missed out today."

National Australia Bank led the way, reaching a record high of A$16.96 before easing to close at A$16.94. ANZ Bank also reached a record high of A$8.46 before easing by the close, its shares ending 13 cents higher at A$8.44.
Shares in Australia's largest grocery retailer, Woolworths Ltd closed four cents higher at A$3.39 after its 8.6 percent higher first half net profit of A$147.5 million.
Soft drink maker C-C Amatil Ltd shares slid 71.7 cents to A$12.94 after the company's soft year net profit of A$142.1 million, reported after the market closed on Friday.
Golden Valley Mines topped volumes with 21.19 million shares traded after reports a settlement over the controversial Indonesian Busang gold deposit was imminent.
Golden Valley shares closed 1.5 cents higher at A$0.115.
Turnover by value was dominated by Commonwealth Bank with active ex-dividend trade totalling 11.46 million shares worth A$145.22 million.
Woodside Petroleum shares rose 19 cents to A$9.31, after the company said it was to announce an upgrade in gas reserves at the North-West Shelf to 24 trillion cubic feet (tcf) from about 15 tcf.
Shares in aluminium producer Comalco Ltd slipped 16 cents to A$6.70 after the company said it had abandoned plans to expand its smelting division.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about four to three, while about 31 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Options trade lacked any trader interest but futures trade saw moderate activity.
Total options traded 22,113 (36,631)
Turnover in March SPI contract totalled 5,459 (7,233)

In other local markets, Australian bond futures pared their initial U.S. inspired advance as the market found few takers as the 10-year bond contract struck a two-month high. By 5.00 p.m. (0600 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.27 percent.

A cautious Australian dollar spent the day avoiding testing either resistance and support, awaiting Tuesday's RBA report on the economy from the Reserve Bank of Australia's (RBA). By 5.00 p.m. (0600 GMT), the unit was at US$0.7640/50 from an early US$0.7642/47, having traded a US$0.7637-50 range on the day.
